name: Citizenship by Birth in Territory or by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: Law No. 1968-LF-3 (Cameroon Nationality Code): a legitimate child born of a Cameroonian father OR a Cameroonian mother acquires Cameroonian nationality automatically -- explicitly gender-symmetric on descent. A right to renounce exists within 6 months before reaching majority in certain mixed-parentage cases.
requirements.fix_path: Establish a parental link to a Cameroonian father or mother via a birth certificate.

requirement_groups.name: Born in Cameroon to unknown parents, or foreign-born with a Cameroon-born parent

requirements.blocker_text: A child born in Cameroon to unknown parents acquires nationality, and a found infant discovered in Cameroon is presumed born there. Separately, a foreign-born child may claim nationality if both the child AND at least one parent were themselves born in Cameroon, subject to the same renunciation rights as the standard descent route.
requirements.fix_path: Establish birth in Cameroon to unknown parents (or foundling status), or the two-generation Cameroon-birth link for a foreign-born applicant.

evidence_required.document: Birth certificate showing parental link or place of birth

sources.title: Refworld (UNHCR-hosted primary legal text, English translation) -- Law No. 1968-LF-3, Cameroon Nationality Code: descent rule, birth-in-territory rule, foundling presumption

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Cameroon). STATUS: DRAFT -- read directly from a genuine primary legal text (an English translation of the 1968 Nationality Code, hosted on Refworld), but Refworld is tier 2 by this dataset's own tiering rules, and the validator requires tier-1 (government) sourcing for a hard requirement before a route can be published. No Cameroonian government-hosted copy of the Nationality Code text could be reached in this build, so this file stays draft despite the underlying legal finding being solid. GENUINE, POSITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING: descent is explicitly gender-symmetric ('a Cameroonian father or a Cameroonian mother'), unlike Iraq's asymmetric Articles 3/4 found earlier in this dataset. dual_citizenship_allowed set to false as the general default: the source describes only 'limited provisions favoring dual citizenship,' mainly a temporary automatic extension to minor children during a parent's naturalization process, with renunciation expected otherwise -- not a general allowance, so this dataset does not present it as a blanket yes.
